Image 1: Seven-panel storyboard reference, used for the overall shot structure, shot sizes, and camera-movement rhythm. Read it from left to right and from top to bottom; panel N is Shot N. It is a line-art sketch: do not adopt its sketch style, black outlines, white background, panel borders or drawn faces.
Image 2: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the front view, the establishing view, facing the back wall, a rendered set, not live action. Use it only for the room's layout, the furniture's positions and the light's direction; do not reference its visual content. It contains no people.
Image 3: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the back view, turned 180 degrees, facing the front wall, with the left wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 4: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the left-side view, facing the left wall, with the back wall at its right edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 5: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the right-side view, facing the right wall, with the back wall at its left edge, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 6: Reference of Sebastian's apartment, living room, the floor plan seen from above: its top edge is the back wall, its bottom edge the front wall behind the front view's camera, and its left and right edges the left and right walls, a rendered set, used only for the room's layout; it contains no people.
Image 7: Blocking reference of the segment's start: the same place with these people in their places, used only for where each person is and which way they face; take faces and outfits from each subject's own image. It is a line-art diagram: do not adopt its outlines or white background.
Image 8: Subject 1 (Natalie, look S2) character appearance reference.
Image 9: Subject 2 (Sebastian, look S3) character appearance reference.
Image 10: Prop 1 (Sebastian's phone) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 10.
Image 11: Prop 2 (agreement) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 11.
Image 12: Prop 3 (pillow) maps to this image; use only structure, material, and color, and copy its writing and badges exactly from Image 12.
[Subject settings]
Subject 1 (Natalie): Refer to Image 8. 25, the heroine; George's daughter from his first marriage, who agrees to marry Sebastian Klein to pay for her mother's dialysis. Outfit: look S2: Sleepwear: an opaque powder-blue silk camisole with thin straps, a modest V neckline trimmed in ivory lace and a softly fitted waist. Matching opaque powder-blue silk sleep shorts with lace-trimmed hems. Over them, an ivory-white satin knee-length robe with long sleeves, worn open, with its sash hanging loose. Barefoot. Hair loose in soft curls. Signature colour: blue.
Subject 2 (Sebastian): Refer to Image 9. 30, the hero; the scorned illegitimate son of the Klein family, jailed for three days for reckless driving and secretly a billionaire running a plan. Outfit: look S3: Night at home: a fitted white ribbed sleeveless undershirt that shows his broad shoulders and athletic arms, loose black cotton lounge trousers, and bare feet. The wristwatch is still on. Signature colour: black.
Environment (Sebastian's apartment, living room): Refer to Images 2 to 6. Night, warm lamplight indoors, city lights glowing through the window. Warm arc floor lamp and the pendant over the dining table; the phone screen casts a cool glow on Sebastian's face. Quiet room tone, a phone buzz.
Do not swap the characters' appearances, clothing, actions, positions or dialogue.
[Subjects and relationships]
Only two people appear throughout: Natalie and Sebastian.
[Blocking]
Refer to Images 2 to 6 for the room and Image 7 for the people's places. Natalie stands in the bedroom doorway on the back wall in her camisole, sleep shorts and open robe, one hand on the door. Sebastian, in his white undershirt, stands one step in front of her outside the bedroom door. His phone lies face down on the round coffee table beside the signed agreement; the pillow lies at the front-door end of the couch.
[Overall style]
Photorealistic live-action short drama with cinematic lighting. Each character keeps the face and the outfit with its main colour from their reference image throughout. Use each character sheet only for that character: the face from the close-up on the right, the body and outfit from the turnaround on the left; do not render the sheet's layout, white background or multiple views. This segment has no dialogue; nobody speaks. Generate speech only from the lines in {} in the shot list, each spoken exactly once by its speaker; everyone else keeps their mouth naturally closed while listening, and a V.O. speaker keeps their mouth closed or is off screen. Follow the shot list below; do not add cuts or camera moves beyond it. Strictly adhere to the 180-degree rule: within a scene, characters keep their screen sides and the camera stays on one side of the axis. Seamless continuity of action, spatial matching and consistent actor blocking; cut on action. For dialogue prefer static shot-reverse-shot and over-the-shoulder shots, balanced with reaction shots and close-up inserts. Faces stable and clear, consistent with the reference images, with no resemblance to any real actor or actress. Normal human eyes. Natural anatomy and hands. Natural, fluid motion that follows the blocking; characters make subtle, natural movements. Characters, props and environment share one world with matched lighting. Each line ends naturally with breathing room and is never cut off. Authentic performances with micro-expressions. No BGM; generate only dialogue, environmental sounds and action sounds. No subtitles.
[Continuity]
Maintain continuity in the identities, number, appearance, clothing, relative heights, spatial positions, and eyelines of all the characters. The actions in the shot list occur strictly in sequence. Hands are anatomically correct.
[Strictly exclude]
garbled or wrong text on the phone screen. added or missing characters, spatial jumps. subtitles. Dialogue from the wrong character, multiple people speaking at once, repeated or missing lines, lip-sync errors and audio-visual desynchronization. The raw reference images (character sheets, setting plates) appearing as a frame of the video, and starting on a still frame of the setting reference. A fast zoom-in at the start, a fast pull-back at the end, unmotivated whip-pans, tilts, zooms and 360-degree orbits. Axis-crossing, jump cuts, frame skips, flicker and clipping. Face swaps, changes in age or clothing, sudden height shifts, added or missing characters, spatial jumps, and disordered action sequences; props popping in or vanishing, and duplicate characters except mirror reflections. Hand clipping, extra fingers, fused fingers, malformed hands. Subtitles, captions, watermarks and garbled writing; writing and logos other than those on a key prop's reference image, which are copied from it; a phone screen or paper that is not a key prop is shown from the back or out of focus. Black-and-white, monochrome, grayscale, desaturated visuals; hand-drawn, sketch, line art, illustration, comics, animation; storyboard frames, rough sketches, panel borders, gutters and grid layouts.
[Shot list] (7 shots, approximately 15 seconds)
When a previous-shot reference image is given, it is the moment this segment starts from: keep its people's positions, outfits, props and light, and continue from there. Shot 1 keeps its own camera, matching the image's framing only when it frames the same view; do not repeat that frame later.
Shot 1 (0-2s): [Medium shot, eye-level, past Sebastian's shoulder toward the bedroom door] Natalie gives him a last look and closes the bedroom door between them. <Bedroom door clicks shut>
Shot 2 (2-4s): [Wide shot, locked-off, eye-level, from the kitchenette side; closed bedroom door at frame right] Sebastian walks from the closed bedroom door back to the couch and sits at its kitchenette end. <Couch creaks>
Shot 3 (4-6s): [Close-up insert, high angle, on the coffee table] Sebastian's black phone lights up on the coffee table beside the signed agreement. <Phone buzzes on wood>
Shot 4 (6-8s): [Medium close-up, low angle, on Sebastian on the couch] Sebastian picks up the phone and taps open the notification, his face turning calm and focused in its glow.
Shot 5 (8-11s): [Close-up, over-the-shoulder shot past Sebastian onto the phone screen, high angle] The phone screen shows the private-banking notification on its dark background, as in the prop reference.
Shot 6 (11-13s): [Close-up insert, high angle, on the coffee table] Sebastian's hand slides the phone face down beneath the signed agreement. <Paper whispers over glass>
Shot 7 (13-15s): [Medium shot, slow pull out from Sebastian, eye-level, closed bedroom door in the background] Sebastian leans back on the couch, glances at the closed bedroom door and gives a faint smile.
At the end: Natalie is inside the bedroom behind the closed bedroom door on the back wall. Sebastian, in his white undershirt, sits leaning back at the kitchenette end of the couch. His phone lies hidden beneath the signed agreement on the round coffee table; the pillow lies at the front-door end of the couch.

<Image 13> is the previous shot (seg03/t02 at 27.96s).
